blocks.en: Assume that $f\in L^1((0,T),H)$, $u_0\in V$, $u_1\in H$ and that $A$ is as described above. Then there exists a unique weak solution $u\in C([0,T],V)\cap C^1([0,T],H)$ of the evolution problem \eqref{eq:abstract-hyperbolic-evolution-initial-value-problem}.
blocks.zh: 假设 $f\in L^1((0,T),H)$, $u_0\in V$, $u_1\in H$, 且 $A$ 如上所述. 则演化问题 \eqref{eq:abstract-hyperbolic-evolution-initial-value-problem} 存在唯一弱解 $u\in C([0,T],V)\cap C^1([0,T],H)$.
blocks.label: thm:abstract-hyperbolic-existence-uniqueness

source_locations.bbox_precision: visually selected parent block, top-left PDF points

blocks.en: For the proof, we shall need to proceed in several steps. We shall first give a proof of existence. This proof is similar in spirit to the one given in the previous section for parabolic problems. We first derive an energy equation which yields an a priori estimate for a solution. Then we use an approximation scheme and uniform energy estimates to obtain a solution as a weak limit. The energy estimate yields uniqueness only if more regularity of the solution is assumed; we shall therefore need a separate argument to prove uniqueness. Finally, the existence proof we give will only show that the solution is in $L^\infty((0,T),V)\cap W^{1,\infty}((0,T),H)$, and a separate argument is needed to establish continuity.\par We remark that if $u$ has the regularity guaranteed by the theorem, it does not follow that $f\in L^1((0,T),H)$. Hyperbolic problems differ from parabolic problems in the fact that they lack coercive properties; solutions are not ``as smooth as the data will allow.\textquotesingle\textquotesingle\ This makes these problems in many respects harder than parabolic equations.
blocks.zh: 证明需要分几步进行. 首先证明存在性. 这一证明的思路与前一节对抛物型问题给出的证明相似. 首先导出一个能量方程, 由它得到解的先验估计. 再利用近似方案和一致能量估计, 将解作为弱极限得到. 只有在假设解具有更高正则性时, 该能量估计才能给出唯一性; 因此还需单独论证唯一性. 最后, 所给的存在性证明只能说明解属于 $L^\infty((0,T),V)\cap W^{1,\infty}((0,T),H)$, 还需单独论证连续性.\par 注意, 即使 $u$ 具有该定理所保证的正则性, 也不能推出 $f\in L^1((0,T),H)$. 双曲型问题与抛物型问题的区别在于前者缺乏强制性; 解并不是 ``数据允许有多光滑就有多光滑\textquotesingle\textquotesingle. 这使得这些问题在许多方面比抛物型方程更难.

blocks.en: We already know that $u\in C([0,T],H)$ and $\dot u\in C([0,T],V^*)$. The following lemma allows us to draw a further conclusion from this:
blocks.zh: 已经知道 $u\in C([0,T],H)$ 和 $\dot u\in C([0,T],V^*)$. 下面的引理允许由此得到进一步的结论:

source_locations.bbox_precision: visually selected parent block, top-left PDF points

blocks.en: Let $V$ and $H$ be Hilbert spaces such that $V$ is continuously and densely imbedded in $H$. Assume that $u\in L^\infty((0,T),V)\cap C([0,T],H)$. Then $u(t)\in V$ for every $t\in[0,T]$ and $u(t)$ is weakly continuous; i.e., $(f,u(t))$ is a continuous function of $t$ for every $f\in V^*$.
blocks.zh: 设 $V$ 和 $H$ 为 Hilbert 空间, 且 $V$ 连续并稠密地嵌入于 $H$. 假设 $u\in L^\infty((0,T),V)\cap C([0,T],H)$. 则对每个 $t\in[0,T]$, 都有 $u(t)\in V$, 且 $u(t)$ 弱连续; 即对每个 $f\in V^*$, $(f,u(t))$ 都是 $t$ 的连续函数.
blocks.label: lem:hilbert-triple-weak-continuity

source_locations.bbox_precision: visually selected parent block, top-left PDF points
visually selected parent block, top-left PDF points

blocks.en: Using the lemma, we conclude that the solution $u$ of \eqref{eq:abstract-parabolic-form-coercivity} is weakly continuous with values in $V$ and $\dot u$ is weakly continuous with values in $H$.
blocks.zh: 利用该引理, 可知 \eqref{eq:abstract-parabolic-form-coercivity} 的解 $u$ 作为 $V$ 值函数弱连续, 而 $\dot u$ 作为 $H$ 值函数弱连续.

blocks.en: Establish an existence and uniqueness result for the following perturbation of \eqref{eq:abstract-hyperbolic-evolution-initial-value-problem}: $\ddot u=A(t)u+B(t)u$, where $A$ is as above and $B$ is a bounded operator from $V$ to $H$.
